title: Lipschitz images of countably n-rectifiable sets are countably n-rectifiable
statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Λ ≥ 0, E := ℝ^P (Euclid P) and H^n := μHE[n]. Let φ : E → E be Λ-Lipschitz, and let M ⊆ E be any set, not assumed measurable. Suppose M is countably n-rectifiable in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.1 (CountablyRectifiable n M): there are M₀ ⊆ E with H^n(M₀) = 0 and maps F_j : ℝ^n → E (j ∈ ℕ), each Lipschitz with some constant, such that M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n). Then φ(M) is countably n-rectifiable.
lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (φ : Euclid P → Euclid P) (Λ : NNReal), LipschitzWith Λ φ → CountablyRectifiable n M → CountablyRectifiable n (φ '' M)
